questions.question: What is ‘Mahawat’ in India?

options.text: Cold waves during the winter season
Cloud burst during the monsoon season
Cyclonic rainfall during the winter season
Hot and dry winds during the summer season

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3) Cyclonic rainfall during the winter season**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahawat** refers to **cyclonic rainfall** that occurs during the **winter season** in India.
 
• These cyclonic rains are generally caused by western disturbances that originate in the Mediterranean region and bring moisture-laden winds to the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Such rainfall is crucial for the **Rabi crops**, especially wheat, as it provides essential moisture during the growing period.
 
• Western disturbances typically affect the northern parts of India, including Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Western disturbances** are low-pressure systems that move from west to east and are more frequent in the winter months.
 
• These disturbances can also cause a drop in temperatures, leading to cold wave conditions in the affected regions.
 
• The term **'Mahawat'** is commonly used in the agricultural context in India, emphasizing its importance to winter crops.
 
• Besides agricultural benefits, heavy cyclonic rainfall can sometimes lead to localized flooding and disruption in daily activities.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India deals with the organization of village panchayat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 40**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 40** of the Constitution of India deals with the **organization of village panchayats**.
 
• It falls under **Part IV** of the Constitution, which contains the **Directive Principles of State Policy**.
 
• This article directs the state to organize village panchayats and endow them with powers and authority to function as units of self-government.
 
• The aim is to promote decentralization and empower local self-governance in rural areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are guidelines to the central and state governments of India to be kept in mind while framing laws and policies.
 
• They are** not justiciable in a court of law** but are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• The aim of these principles is to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They emphasize that the state should strive to promote the welfare of the people by securing and protecting a social order in which justice—social, economic, and political—shall inform all institutions of national life.
 
• The **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**, further strengthened the role of **Panchayati Raj Institutions **(PRIs) by giving them constitutional status.

questions.question: Bharati Shivaji and Kanak Rele are exponents of ______.

• **Mohiniyattam** is known for its graceful and gentle movements, often described as the dance of the enchantress.
 
• This dance form traditionally involves themes of love and devotion, and its repertoire includes various elements such as the Cholkettu, Varnam, Padam, and Tillana.
 
• **Bharati Shivaji** has been instrumental in the revival of Mohiniyattam and has received numerous awards for her contributions.
 
• **Kanak Rele** is a pioneer in the field of Mohiniyattam and has established the Nalanda Dance Research Centre, which focuses on the research and promotion of Indian classical dance forms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mohiniyattam** is one of the eight classical dance forms of India recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.
 
• The name **Mohiniyattam** derives from 'Mohini', a mythical enchantress avatar of the Hindu god Vishnu, and 'attam', meaning dance.
 
• This dance form is characterized by its elegant costumes, typically a white or off-white sari with a gold border, and distinctive jewelry.
 
• It is performed mainly by women and is marked by its fluid, feminine movements and subtle facial expressions.

questions.question: Which is the most common ore of oxidised mercury that occurs in granular crusts or veins associated with volcanic activity and hot springs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cinnabar**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cinnabar** is the most common ore of oxidised **mercury **that occurs in granular crusts or veins associated with volcanic activity and hot springs.
 
• Cinnabar is a bright red mineral consisting of **mercury sulfide (HgS)**.
 
• It has been used historically as a pigment and is the primary source of mercury.
 
• The mineral forms in a variety of geological environments, often in association with volcanic activity and hot springs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mercury** has various industrial applications, including in thermometers, barometers, and other scientific instruments.
 
• **Exposure to mercury** and its compounds can be highly toxic, affecting the nervous system, digestive system, and immune system.
 
• The extraction and processing of cinnabar to produce mercury must be handled with extreme care to prevent environmental contamination and health hazards.
 
• The use of mercury has declined due to its toxicity and the development of safer alternatives.

questions.question: Who is regarded as the ‘Mother of Indian Revolution’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madame Cama**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Madame Cama** is widely regarded as the '**Mother of Indian Revolution**'.
 
• She was an important figure in the Indian independence movement and played a crucial role in advocating for India's freedom from British rule.
 
• Madame Cama was known for her fiery speeches and was deeply involved in the revolutionary activities against the British Empire.
 
• She also **unfurled the first version of the Indian national flag in 1907 **at the **International Socialist Conference in Stuttgart, Germany.**
 
• Her contributions to the freedom struggle were significant, and she inspired many young revolutionaries to join the cause.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• She was a strong advocate for gender equality and worked tirelessly for the upliftment of women in society.
 
• Madame Cama was influenced by the social and political conditions of her time and was determined to fight against the injustices perpetrated by the British colonial rulers.
 
• She spent a significant part of her life in exile in Europe, where she continued her revolutionary activities and garnered international support for India's independence.
 
• Madame Cama passed away on 13th August 1936, but her legacy continues to inspire generations of Indians.

questions.concept: Ecology and Functions of an ecosystem
questions.question: Which microscopic, single-celled photosynthetic organisms are known as the primary producers of the ocean - the organisms that form the base of the aquatic food chains?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phytoplankton**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Phytoplankton** are microscopic, **single-celled photosynthetic organisms** that are considered the primary producers of the ocean.
 
• They form the base of the aquatic food chains, supporting a wide range of marine life from tiny zooplankton to large whales.
 
• These organisms use sunlight to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen through the process of photosynthesis.
 
• Phytoplankton are crucial for the marine ecosystem as they generate approximately half of the Earth's oxygen and serve as a major sink for carbon dioxide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zooplankton** are heterotrophic and feed on phytoplankton and other small organisms; they are not primary producers.
 
• **Bacterioplankton** consist of bacteria that play a role in recycling nutrients in the marine environment, but they are not primary producers.
 
• **Virioplankton** are viruses that infect marine organisms, including bacteria and plankton; they do not contribute to primary production.
 
• Phytoplankton populations are influenced by factors such as light availability, nutrient levels, and water temperature.

questions.question: What is the name of the geographic feature that serves as a boundary between Europe and Africa?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Strait of Gibraltar**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Strait of Gibraltar **lies between the **southern tip of Spain (Europe) and the northern tip of Morocco (Africa)**.
 
• It **connects the Atlantic Ocean to the Mediterranean Sea** and** separates Southern Spain in Europe from Northern Morocco in Africa**.
 
• It is strategically important as it serves as the gateway between the Mediterranean Sea and the Atlantic Ocean.
 
• This strait has been a significant maritime route for centuries, facilitating **trade** and cultural exchange between Europe and Africa.
 
• It is** one of the busiest maritime routes** in the world, with both commercial ships and naval vessels passing through it regularly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/149749c2bf2426fe542db7371aafa4fb9c5eb59e39271ec4c0793a2c7e563c4a.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Bosporus Strait** connects the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara and separates Europe from Asia in Turkey.
 
• The **Dardanelles Strait** also in Turkey, connects the Aegean Sea to the Sea of Marmara.
 
• The **Malacca Strait** is located between the Malay Peninsula and the Indonesian island of Sumatra, connecting the Pacific Ocean to the Indian Ocean.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of microfinance institutions (MFIs) in India?

options.text: To promote consumer spending among middle-class households
To offer financial services exclusively to large businesses
To provide small loans to low-income individuals
To facilitate foreign investment in the Indian economy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**to provide small loans to low-income individuals**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Microfinance institutions (MFIs)** primarily aim to provide **small loans** to low-income individuals who do not have access to traditional banking services.
 
• These institutions play a crucial role in **financial inclusion** by offering credit to those who are typically excluded from the formal financial system.
 
• MFIs help in empowering **economically disadvantaged groups**, especially women, by providing them with the necessary capital to start or expand small businesses.
 
• They contribute to **poverty alleviation** and promote **entrepreneurship** at the grassroots level.
 
• MFIs also offer other financial services such as savings, insurance, and remittance services to their clients.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Microfinance in India has its roots in the **Self-Help Group (SHG)** movement, which started in the 1980s.
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** regulates MFIs to ensure they operate within a framework that protects the interests of borrowers.
 
• MFIs operate under various models, including the **Grameen model** and the **Self-Help Group (SHG) model**.
 
• The growth of the microfinance sector in India has led to the establishment of several **Microfinance Institutions Network (MFIN)** and **Sa-Dhan**, which are industry associations that promote best practices and advocate for the sector.
 
• Despite the benefits, the microfinance sector has faced challenges such as high-interest rates, over-indebtedness, and issues related to loan recovery practices.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about transfer payments in relation to personal income?

options.text: Transfer payments are included in personal income.
Transfer payments have no impact on personal income.
Transfer payments are included in personal income only for businesses.
Transfer payments are excluded from personal income

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**transfer payments are included in personal income**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Transfer payments are included in personal income.** This means that when calculating personal income, transfer payments such as social security benefits, unemployment compensation, and welfare payments are added.
 
• Transfer payments are a significant component of personal income, especially for individuals who rely on government assistance.
 
• These payments are not in exchange for goods or services provided and do not represent earned income, but they still contribute to the overall personal income of individuals.
 
• Including transfer payments in personal income provides a more comprehensive understanding of an individual's total income resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Personal income** is the total income received by individuals and households before paying personal taxes.
 
• It includes wages, salaries, bonuses, social security benefits, dividends, interest, rental income, and transfer payments.
 
• Transfer payments are typically funded through taxation and are aimed at redistributing wealth to provide financial support to individuals in need.
 
• Understanding the role of transfer payments in personal income is crucial for analyzing economic policies and their impact on income distribution and poverty alleviation.

questions.question: Bharhut Stupa is located in which of the following states?

__
 
• **Bharhut Stupa** is located in the state of **Madhya Pradesh**, India.
 
• The stupa is a significant example of early Indian Buddhist art and architecture.
 
• It dates back to the **2nd century BCE** during the Shunga period.
 
• The site is known for its intricate carvings and detailed sculptures that depict Jataka tales and various Buddhist motifs.
 
• Many of the sculptures from Bharhut Stupa are now housed in museums, including the Indian Museum in Kolkata.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Bharhut Stupa** was discovered by the British archaeologist **Alexander Cunningham** in the 19th century.
 
• The stupa originally stood in the town of Bharhut, now in the **Satna district** of Madhya Pradesh.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of the fundamental rights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 32**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 32** of the Constitution of India **guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of the fundamental rights**.
 
• This Article is often referred to as the "**heart and soul" of the Constitution** by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
 
• It ensures that individuals have the right to approach the highest court directly in case of any violation of their fundamental rights.
 
• Under this Article, the Supreme Court has the authority to issue directions or orders or writs, including writs in the nature of habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari, whichever may be appropriate, for the enforcement of any of the rights conferred by Part III of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26th November 1949 and came into effect on 26th January 1950.
 
• It is the longest written constitution of any country in the world and lays down the framework defining fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• Article 32 is a crucial part of the Constitution as it empowers the Supreme Court to ensure that the rights guaranteed to citizens are protected and enforced.
 
• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar described Article 32 as the most important article of the Constitution, without which the Constitution would be a nullity.
 
• This Article is a testament to the commitment of the Indian Constitution to uphold the fundamental rights of its citizens.
